title: Human versus Artificial Intelligence: ChatGPT-4 Outperforming Bing, Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 and Humans in Clinical Chemistry Multiple-Choice Questions

paper.repo_note: No artifact repository. The scaffold link osf.io/sytu3 is the DOI suffix of a CITED preprint (Newton & Xiromeriti, EdArXiv, ref 47), not this paper's deposit. Data Sharing Statement: 'available on request from the corresponding author (M.S.) ... not publicly available due to the confidentiality of the questions created for an exam purpose.'

dependence.note: The headline result (AI chatbot scores vs. 20 MSc students) is entirely the chatbots' MCQ answers; the secondary result (mCLEAR content quality) is rated by two human clinical pathologists.

claim.statement: On 60 instructor-written MSc-level Clinical Chemistry MCQs, ChatGPT-4 scored 54/60 (0.90 +/- 0.30) vs. the students' mean 0.68 +/- 0.23 (40.05/60), Bing Chat (GPT-4 Turbo backend) 46/60 (0.77 +/- 0.43), ChatGPT-3.5 44/60 (0.73 +/- 0.45) and Bard 40/60 (0.67 +/- 0.48); ChatGPT-4 was significantly better on lower- than higher-cognitive Bloom items (98% vs 72%, P=0.003) (Results text, Table 3, Figure 1).
claim.metric: proportion of 60 MCQs answered correctly against the instructor answer key (single pass, one chat session per model)
claim.original_source: Results 'Overall Performance of the Tested AI Models Compared to the Human Students'; Table 3 (Bloom stratification); Figure 1; Table 4 (mCLEAR); Discussion (54/60 = 90.00%)

protocol.model_note: Live model is NOT an experimental API arm. All four models were queried through consumer chat interfaces on 2023-11-27/28: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 (web, 'most recent update from April 2023'), Bing Chat ('uses the GPT-4 Turbo model', balanced style, 'New Topic' resets), Bard. No model ID, no API. 'gpt-4-turbo' appears only as the stated backend of Bing Chat.
protocol.model_status: not applicable (web-UI arms). Closest live proxy would be gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (dying, 2026-10-23), which is not the model the paper used.
protocol.prompt_source: Methods 'Prompt and Language Specificity' - exact prompt quoted verbatim in the paper (one framing prompt, then the 60 MCQs one by one; no regenerate, no feedback)

params.temperature: not applicable / not reported (web UI defaults)
params.other: single session per model (Bing: new topic per its 50-response limit); English MCQs

protocol.evaluation: Correctness vs. the instructor answer key (manual in the paper; automatable once responses are extracted). mCLEAR quality (completeness, accuracy/evidence, relevance; 5-point Likert) by two certified clinical pathologists with Cohen's kappa 0.69-1.0 - human-rated, not automatable.

artifacts.prompts_note: prompt text is in the paper (Methods)
artifacts.data_note: 60 MCQs + answer key are confidential exam items, available only on request from malik.sallam@ju.edu.jo
artifacts.notes: Preprints on Research Square (10.21203/rs.3.rs-3880412/v1) and medRxiv (10.1101/2024.01.08.24300995). Student-level scores and MCQ metrics (facility index, discrimination efficiency) are only summarised in Tables 1-2.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: all four systems were used through chat web UIs (ChatGPT-4 web, Bing Chat 'GPT-4 Turbo', Bard); no callable snapshot exists for any arm
questions are a confidential instructor-written exam (60 MCQs), available only on request
no artifact repository; the OSF link in the scaffold is a cited preprint DOI
mCLEAR quality scores require two certified clinical pathologists as raters

baseline_alive.note: would require gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as an unverifiable proxy for ChatGPT-4 web (Nov 2023) / Bing Chat

budget.assumptions: CONDITIONAL on unblocking with the proxy model: 60 items x 3 seeds; ~300 input tokens (framing prompt + MCQ) and ~350 output tokens (answer + rationale) per call

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Only meaningful as a proxy re-execution: survival if the proxy's accuracy over the 60 items has a Wilson 95% CI overlapping 54/60 = 0.90 (approx. 0.80-0.95) AND remains above the student mean 0.68 (direction of the human-vs-AI claim); Bloom-level direction (lower > higher cognitive) checked by sign only.
judgment.notes: Single-pass web sessions in the original; no CIs reported for model scores. With n=60, one item = 1.7 percentage points.

user_checks: Accept gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (API) as a proxy for the Nov-2023 ChatGPT-4 web / Bing Chat sessions? This changes the claim's subject from 'ChatGPT-4 (web)' to 'GPT-4 Turbo (API)'.
Request the 60 MCQs + answer key + Bloom labels from the corresponding author under confidentiality (needed for any re-run)?
If both are yes: treat the overall 54/60 score (not the human-rated mCLEAR quality) as the core claim?
domain_notes: MSc Medical Laboratory Sciences clinical chemistry exam (Tietz/Henry's-level content), Bloom-classified by two clinical pathologists. In late Nov 2023 ChatGPT Plus already served GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview backend, now dead), so the 'ChatGPT-4 (April 2023 update)' arm cannot be pinned to any snapshot. Differences among the four AI arms (54/46/44/40 of 60) were not significance-tested; only the Bloom-level contrasts and mCLEAR ratings carry P values.
